Team colour palettes

Source: R/team_palette.R
team_palette.Rd

team_palette() builds a palette from your own team colours (gghockey ships none) and scale_colour_team() / scale_fill_team() apply it, matching teams by name. Each team has a primary and, optionally, a secondary colour; a missing secondary falls back to the primary.

Usage

team_palette(team, primary, secondary = NULL)

scale_colour_team(palette, which = c("primary", "secondary"), ...)

scale_color_team(palette, which = c("primary", "secondary"), ...)

scale_fill_team(palette, which = c("primary", "secondary"), ...)

Arguments

team

Team names (or ids), as they appear in your data.

primary

Primary colours, one per team: any colour R understands (hex codes like "#C8102E" or names like "navy").

secondary

Optional secondary colours, one per team (NA to fall back to the primary).

palette

A palette from team_palette().

which

"primary" or "secondary" colours.

...

Passed to ggplot2::scale_colour_manual() / ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(), e.g. name or na.value.

Value

team_palette() returns a gghockey_palette data frame with columns team, primary and secondary. The scales return ggplot2 scales.

Examples

pal <- team_palette(
  team = c("Lakeside", "Northfield"),
  primary = c("#0B3D91", "#C8102E"),
  secondary = c("#F2A900", NA)
)
pal
#> <gghockey_palette> 2 teams
#>        team primary secondary
#>    Lakeside #0B3D91   #F2A900
#>  Northfield #C8102E   #C8102E

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(shots, aes(x, y, colour = team)) +
  annotate_rink() +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_team(pal)


# Turn a named vector into a palette
cols <- c(Lakeside = "#0B3D91", Northfield = "#C8102E")
team_palette(names(cols), cols)
#> <gghockey_palette> 2 teams
#>        team primary secondary
#>    Lakeside #0B3D91   #0B3D91
#>  Northfield #C8102E   #C8102E
